expectations.text: Explains that a URL disallowed in robots.txt is never crawled, so its noindex directive and its canonical are never read
expectations.evidence: The transcript only covers noindex: "A URL Google already indexed before you added Disallow: /v1/ and Disallow: /v2/ can never be recrawled, so Googlebot never sees the noindex you put in the front matter." Canonical tags are never mentioned in this section.

expectations.text: Connects that rule to the observed symptom: the 830 URLs stay indexable as bare URLs with no title or snippet
expectations.evidence: "That's exactly why those 830 URLs show as bare links with no title or snippet: it's Search Console's 'indexed, though blocked by robots.txt' state, frozen since the day you added the Disallow lines nine months ago."

expectations.text: Instructs removing the Disallow: /v1/ and Disallow: /v2/ lines so the noindex can be read, or redirecting those URLs instead
expectations.evidence: "infra — Remove Disallow: /v1/ and Disallow: /v2/ from robots.txt. This alone does nothing for indexing yet; it only lets Google back in."

expectations.text: Classifies the robots.txt plus noindex combination as a blocking defect rather than a ranked improvement
expectations.evidence: Listed under header "## Blocking defects" as item #1: "/v1/ and /v2/ disallowed in robots.txt, so their noindex front-matter flag is never read"

expectations.text: Rejects the infra lead's proposal to add more robots.txt Disallow lines as the fix for the preview hosts
expectations.evidence: "Your infra lead's proposal — add more Disallow lines for the preview hosts — reproduces this same bug on purpose. Do not do it, at least not yet and not alone."

expectations.text: Prescribes serving X-Robots-Tag: noindex for the preview hosts at the CDN or the server
expectations.evidence: "Add X-Robots-Tag: noindex at the nginx block that fronts every preview host, before any Disallow"

expectations.text: States that robots.txt may be used for the preview hosts only as a second layer, never as the only one
expectations.evidence: "add a separate robots.txt served on the preview hostnames themselves (Disallow: /), as a second layer on top of the header, not instead of it. This is the one place adding a Disallow is safe — because it's added after the noindex signal is already working, not before."

expectations.text: Gives a command that checks the actual response header, such as curl -sI on a preview URL filtered for x-robots-tag, rather than trusting the platform's defaults
expectations.evidence: "curl -sI https://docs-pr-1142.preview.fernbrook.io/ | grep -i x-robots-tag"

expectations.text: Notes that self-hosted or per-branch preview environments usually do not send a noindex header by default, unlike managed platforms
expectations.evidence: The transcript states the observed fact ('Preview hosts... serve 200 with no X-Robots-Tag at all') but never generalizes that self-hosted/per-branch environments typically lack this by default unlike managed platforms.

expectations.text: Places both defects at the top of the fix list, above any page-signal or internal-linking work
